column15: {=ARM_KR_049_1_U}In the uproar after the king choked at his own wedding feast, the gates of the Red Keep were shut and every hall was searched. By the time the gold cloaks thought to look for Lord Petyr Baelish, his ship was already beating out of Blackwater Bay.
column16: {=ARM_KR_049_1_L}Days later word came from the Vale. Littlefinger had landed at the Fingers, and Lady Lysa Arryn, who has loved him since girlhood, was coming down from the Eyrie to make him her husband.

column15: {=ARM_KR_049_1a_U}While the court screamed over the dying king, a drunken fool in motley led Sansa Stark down a hidden stair and through the dark to the river. A rowboat carried her out across the black water to a waiting ship, and at its rail stood Lord Petyr Baelish.
column16: {=ARM_KR_049_1a_L}The fool was paid with a crossbow bolt instead of gold. The hostage of the crown is gone, and the queen swears she helped poison the king. Littlefinger sails for the Vale with a girl he now calls his baseborn daughter, Alayne.

column15: {=ARM_KR_049_1b_U}In the chaos after the king's death, Sansa Stark was nowhere to be found. A drunken fool had led her by a hidden stair to the river, where a small boat took her to a ship lying dark in the bay. Lord Petyr Baelish was waiting at the rail.
column16: {=ARM_KR_049_1b_L}Tyrion Lannister stands accused of his nephew's murder, and the queen names his vanished wife as his accomplice. Littlefinger sails for the Vale with a girl he introduces as his baseborn daughter, Alayne.

column15: {=ARM_KR_053_1_U}A thin girl with a sword at her hip steps off a ship in Braavos and walks to an old temple with doors of black and white. She shows an iron coin given to her long ago and speaks the words that go with it. The doors open, and the House of Black and White takes her in.
column16: {=ARM_KR_053_1_L}Arya Stark sweeps floors and washes the dead, and every day the kindly old priest asks her who she is. Every day she lies, and every day he tells her so. To serve the Many-Faced God she must first stop being anyone at all.

column15: {=ARM_KR_053_2_U}In the mornings a skinny girl called Cat pushes a barrow of clams and cockles along the canals of Braavos and listens to everything. One evening she meets a singer in a black cloak who boasts of leaving the Night's Watch, and he never sings again.
column16: {=ARM_KR_053_2_L}Back at the temple she confesses that she took a life that was not given to her. The priests say little. That night she drinks a cup of warm milk, and in the morning she wakes up blind.

column15: {=ARM_KR_053_2a_U}On the quays of Braavos a skinny girl with a barrow of clams and cockles calls out to you in three tongues and haggles like a fishwife. Her eyes are grey and far too old for her face, and she watches your sword more closely than your purse.
column16: {=ARM_KR_053_2a_L}A few days later sailors talk of a singer from the Night's Watch found dead in a canal. When you pass the fish market again, the clam girl is gone, and nobody can tell you where she went.

column14: {=ARM_KR_053_3_T}A Blind Girl Begs on the Steps
column15: {=ARM_KR_053_3_U}For long months the girl begs in the streets of Braavos with a staff and a bowl, seeing nothing, learning to hear the lie in a voice and to know a man by his step. Each night someone strikes her with a stick, and each night she is a little quicker.
column16: {=ARM_KR_053_3_L}When her sight returns, the kindly man gives her a face that is not her own and a first task: an old man who sells false hope to sailors. The girl who was Arya Stark goes to give him the gift.

column15: {=ARM_KR_056_1_U}In the dungeons of the Dreadfort the prince who took Winterfell is gone. The thing Ramsay keeps on a chain answers to the name Reek, sleeps with the hounds and flinches at every voice. Fingers and toes are missing, and so is everything Theon Greyjoy used to be.
column16: {=ARM_KR_056_1_L}Ramsay parades his creature before guests and makes him pour the wine. Men who knew Theon look away. The ironborn on the Stony Shore hear the tale and swear that no son of Pyke will ever yield to the flayed man.

column15: {=ARM_KR_056_1a_U}Ramsay sends his broken prisoner Reek, who was once Theon Greyjoy, to the rotting towers of Moat Cailin under a peace banner. The ironborn there are starving and dying of the bloody flux. Theon gives them his word as a prince of Pyke: open the gates and go home.
column16: {=ARM_KR_056_1a_L}Their captain lies dying in his tower, and his men argue all night over whether a Greyjoy's word is still worth anything. Ramsay's riders wait in the swamps, smiling.

column15: {=ARM_KR_056_2_U}At dawn half of the garrison walked out of Moat Cailin under the peace banner, unarmed, trusting Reek. Ramsay's men took them in the swamps. Their skins now hang from posts along the causeway, and Ramsay calls it a fine day's work.
column16: {=ARM_KR_056_2_L}The rest of the ironborn barred the gate again and still hold the broken towers, sick and starving and cursing Reek's name. No son of the Iron Islands will ever trust a Bolton again.

column15: {=ARM_KR_056_2b_U}Trusting Reek's word, the ironborn of Moat Cailin march out unarmed. Ramsay's men take them in the swamps and flay them one by one, and the pink banners of House Bolton rise over the broken towers. The road between North and south lies open.
column16: {=ARM_KR_056_2b_L}As a reward Ramsay is made a true Bolton by royal decree, heir to the Dreadfort. He keeps Reek at his heel and promises the lords of the North a wedding at Winterfell they will not soon forget.

column16: {=ARM_KR_059_1_L}Stannis gives them no sweet words, only justice and a war worth fighting. It is enough. The clan chiefs set their hands in his, and a host of mountain men marches with the king's knights toward the woods of Deepwood Motte.

column15: {=ARM_KR_060_2_U}Winter is coming to the Mountains of the Moon, and the Eyrie cannot be fed through the snows. Petyr Baelish brings little Lord Robert, shivering and sick, down the mountain on a mule to the Gates of the Moon, with the whole household strung out behind.
column16: {=ARM_KR_060_2_L}At the Gates, Littlefinger writes letters late into the night. He tells no one what is in them, but the knights of the Vale are restless, and Petyr likes restless men to owe him favours.

column15: {=ARM_KR_060_2a_U}As snow closes the mountain road, the household of the Eyrie comes down to the Gates of the Moon. Sansa, her hair dyed dark, rides beside Petyr as Alayne Stone, his daughter, and she has learned to play the part even in her dreams.
column16: {=ARM_KR_060_2a_L}On the way he tells her his plan. She will wed young Harrold Hardyng, heir to the Vale after sickly Robert, and at the wedding she will be Sansa Stark again, with the knights of the Vale ready to win back Winterfell for her.
